Based on the chest X-rays provided, which type of Azygos Lobe is present in this patient's chest radiograph, and what specific feature confirms this classification?
A) Type A, confirmed by the presence of a trigonum parietale located laterally at the pulmonary apex.
B) Type B, confirmed by the vertical path of the mesoazygos visible in the X-ray.
C) Type C, confirmed by the trigonum parietale located medially.
D) Type A, confirmed by the C-shaped appearance of the fissure.
E) Type B, confirmed by the fissure appearing straight or slightly undulated.
F) Type C, confirmed by the azygos vein arch lying at a higher than normal cephalad level.
